text:
Predicates:
TwinOrTriplet(x) ::: If people are twins or triplets.
SpendTime(x) ::: They spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
SameAgeSiblings(x) ::: They have siblings who are the same age.
Complain(x) ::: They complain often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHome(x) ::: They live at home regularly.
StrongBonds(x) ::: They develop strong bonds with their family members.
Premises:
∀x (TwinOrTriplet(x) → SpendTime(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (SameAgeSiblings(x) → TwinOrTriplet(x)) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (Complain(x) → SameAgeSiblings(x)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHome(x) → ¬StrongBonds(x)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
∀x (SpendTime(x) → ¬LiveAtHome(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
(TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ StrongBonds(luke)) ⊕ (¬TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ ¬StrongBonds(luke)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.
Conclusion:
SpendTime(luke) ::: Luke spends a lot of time hanging out and playing with his siblings.
